**Advantage clipping** has been proposed to prevent destructive policy updates caused by erroneous value estimates: negative estimated advantages are clipped to zero, so only better-than-expected trajectories reinforce the policy (https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.06066).

This prevents policy-gradient updates from reducing the probabilities of sampled actions, protecting desirable behavior from being wrongly discouraged by inaccurate value estimates; the authors primarily recommend it for stabilizing training in high-variance environments (https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.06066).
